newsitem.title: UK: Brazil aims to retire all Brady debt eventually.
newsitem.headline: Brazil aims to retire all Brady debt eventually.

text.p: Brazil aims to slowly retire all of its outstanding Brady bond debt -- currently at around $40 billion -- a central bank official told Reuters at a conference on Wednesday.

"Our intention is to retire all of the Brady bonds from the market," Jose Linaldo Gomes de Aguiar, head of the Brazilian central bank's external debt department said. But he said he could not put a time frame on how long it would take to do so.
In an effort to "forget the past" he said Brazil would like to move from the Brady market to "more conventional" uncollateralized bonds.
He said the country's recent Brady swap deal was the first step towards this so-called "new phase".

On June 4 Brazil launched a $3.0 billion 30-year global bond. The deal retired around $2.3 billion in Brady bonds, named after U.S. Treasury secretary Nicholas Brady in 1989 who proposed the concept of bonds backed by the U.S. Treasury but with actual repayments being made by a sovereign lesser developed country.
Brazil exchanged around $1.65 billion in principal amount for discount bonds, $500 million for pars and $95 million for Cs, Aguiar said.
It also sold around $750 million of the global bond for cash.
"Our objectives were to establish a liquid 30-year benchmark, exchange restructured debt for new instruments and forget the past," Aguiar said.
He said Brazil was also planning a 10-year sterling denominated Eurobond in the near future.
